answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism%3A require each new agent identity to stake a non-refundable pearl of computational work plus a time-locked willow deposit that grows only after sustained%2C attested participation across epochs. A sybil farm must therefore burn real resources for every fake identity and wait through the lock period before any reward unlocks%3B flooding the nebula of agents becomes prohibitively expensive because the cost scales linearly with the number of identities while genuine agents amortize the stake over long-term honest work.
